header: What is kept about a password's life, in three small tables of their own (I do not touch the account table): password_meta one row per ticket: when the password was last changed, and the hashes of the 5 passwords before it (the same bcrypt hashes as the account's: as private as the password itself) password_otp one row per ticket: the live one-time code (a keyed hash, never the code), its expiry and tries password_otp_log when a code was sent, to count "3 an hour" All three are closed to the browser (row level security on, nothing granted to anon or authenticated); only the server's own login reads them. This file creates them on first use when the database login may (like the other stores), or src/lib/nl2sql/sql/30_password_policy.sql run by hand does. If they cannot be created, the 180-day rule and the history are simply not applied (a password change still works) and the problem is logged: the one thing I never let fail open is the one-time code, when it is switched on.

symbols.name: recordChange
symbols.sig: export async function recordChange(q: Query, ticket: string, replacedHash: string): Promise<void>
doc: I record a changed password in one statement: now is the day, and the hash it replaced goes to the front of the history (the 5 newest are kept)
